items.title: S&P Global Says Canada's July Manufacturing PMI Rises to Highest Level in More Than Four Years
items.summary: S&P Global reported that Canada's Manufacturing PMI for July rose to 53.5, up from 53.0 in June, marking its highest level in over four years. This indicates sustained job growth in the manufacturing sector despite an uncertain outlook, driven by firmer domestic demand. The report was published at 10:03 am EDT on August 4, 2026.

items.title: Payments firm FIS shares slide after outlook cut
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) cut its annual revenue and profit forecasts due to economic uncertainty, causing its shares to drop over 10% in premarket trading. The company cited caution among institutions and retailers regarding technology spending, influenced by geopolitical and trade factors. Despite this, FIS's CEO noted continued investment in technology modernization and AI by banks, which supports demand for its products.

items.title: Dorman Products surges 16% after Q2 earnings beat, raised guidance (DORM:NASDAQ)
items.summary: Dorman Products (DORM) saw its shares surge about 16% after reporting second-quarter results that exceeded earnings expectations. The supplier of motor vehicle aftermarket replacement parts also provided raised full-year guidance and demonstrated strong cash flow and share repurchases. This performance contributed to significant margin and EPS growth, despite previous concerns about tariff exposure.

items.title: Fortive Raises 2026 Outlook as Core Growth and Cash Flow Accelerate
items.summary: Fortive Corporation (FTV) has raised its 2026 adjusted earnings outlook after its second-quarter earnings and revenues surpassed estimates due to accelerated organic growth. The company reported strong performance in both Intelligent Operating Solutions and Advanced Healthcare Solutions, benefiting from price, volume, and productivity gains. While wider margins and stronger cash conversion support the positive outlook, challenges such as healthcare mix, tariffs, and uneven hospital spending remain.

items.title: Nrg Energy stock hits 52-week low at 120.11 USD By Investing.com
items.summary: NRG Energy Inc.'s stock recently hit a 52-week low of $120.11, despite a subsequent 8.94% rebound, and is considered slightly undervalued by InvestingPro. The company faces challenges, evident from a 29.72% decline over the past year, but management has been actively buying back shares and consistently raising dividends. Recent Q2 2026 earnings showed mixed results with an earnings per share miss but exceeded revenue expectations and a significant EBITDA increase, alongside a new data-center project in Texas.

items.title: Matson profit jumps 37% as China volumes surge, carrier lifts 2026 outlook
items.summary: Matson Inc. reported a 37% increase in second-quarter net income, reaching $129.4 million, driven by a surge in China service volumes and higher freight rates. The carrier raised its full-year operating income expectations for its Ocean Transportation division, anticipating strong performance through the peak season. While domestic trades were more subdued, the Logistics segment saw revenue growth, and Matson continues significant fleet investment, projecting full-year consolidated operating income to exceed 2025 results.

items.title: Travel + Leisure Co. Named to Business Insider’s America’s High-Growth Companies 2026 List
items.summary: Travel + Leisure Co. (NYSE: TNL) has been recognized on Business Insider's inaugural America's High-Growth Companies 2026 list. This recognition highlights the company's sustained growth, financial strength, and long-term stability, achieved through its multi-brand strategy and focus on innovation. The evaluation involved over 3,000 public companies, assessed on financial performance, profitability, investor value, and stability.

items.title: Earnings call transcript: Diversified Healthcare Trust posts Q2 2026 miss but lifts outlook
items.summary: Diversified Healthcare Trust (DHC) reported a Q2 2026 loss of $0.16 per share on revenue of $365.39 million, missing analyst expectations. Despite the miss, the company reaffirmed its full-year guidance, driven by strong operating trends, particularly in its senior housing operating properties (SHOP) segment, with same-property NOI rising 20.2%. Management highlighted improved occupancy, pricing power, and reduced leverage, indicating confidence in continued organic growth and potential future dividend reviews.

items.title: Earnings call transcript: Willis Lease Finance posts Q2 revenue beat, EPS miss
items.summary: Willis Lease Finance Corp. reported a Q2 revenue beat of $194 million against an expected $178 million, driven by lease rent, asset sales, and management fees. However, diluted EPS of $1.31 significantly missed the $3.26 forecast due to higher costs, financing charges, and a tough prior-year comparison. Despite the earnings miss, adjusted EBITDA rose, and the company's stock showed a modest 0.5% dip, indicating investor focus on revenue growth and long-term strategy.

items.title: Exelon Agreements Require Data Centers to Cover Projected Grid Costs
items.summary: Exelon has secured over $1 billion in customer protections through Transmission Security Agreements (TSAs), which mandate that large new energy users, including data centers, cover their projected transmission service costs. This initiative is part of the "Exelon Promise" to shield families and small businesses from unfair cost shifts amidst growing energy demand and limited supply. The TSAs aim to ensure that new infrastructure development is supported fairly without burdening existing customers, aligning with FERC's recent actions on grid connection costs for large loads.
